tenant.identity_basis: The appellant is the sub-tenant who became the direct tenant of the cottage.

landlord.identity_basis: The original landlord who accepted the appellant as direct tenant.

property.value: Cottage at No. 1, Hailey Road, New Delhi
property.identity_basis: The demised premises let to the appellant.

commencement_date.identity_basis: The effective date of the direct tenancy agreement between the landlord and appellant.

evidence.proposition: The premises were let directly by the landlord to the particular applicant tenant with the relevant tenancy commencing after the commencement of the Act.
evidence.application: The Supreme Court recounts that the appellant and landlord reached an agreement effective May 1, 1955, establishing a direct tenancy after the Act's commencement.

R01.P1.basis: Supreme Court's factual reconstruction of the direct tenancy commencement.

petition.value: Section 8 petition for determination of standard rent
petition.identity_basis: The document filed under Section 8 of the Act.

commencement_date.identity_basis: The tenancy commencement date used for the limitation calculation.

filing_date.identity_basis: The date the petition was filed.

evidence.proposition: The applicant filed the Section 8 petition within six months from commencement of that applicant's relevant tenancy.
evidence.application: The Supreme Court notes the filing date (Oct 10, 1955) falls within six months of the direct tenancy commencement (May 1, 1955).

R01.P2.basis: Supreme Court's procedural account of the filing timeline.

head_tenant.identity_basis: The head tenant who inducted the appellant as subtenant.

subtenant.identity_basis: The appellant was inducted as subtenant.

property.value: Cottage at No. 1, Hailey Road, New Delhi
property.identity_basis: The premises subject to the subtenancy.

induction_date.identity_basis: The date of induction as subtenant.

evidence.proposition: The head tenant inducted the appellant as subtenant after the Act commenced.
evidence.stage: classification of tenancy and interpretation of limitation
evidence.application: The Supreme Court recounts that Brook inducted the appellant as a subtenant on September 1, 1954, which was after the Act's commencement.

R02.P1.stage: classification of tenancy and interpretation of limitation
R02.P1.basis: Supreme Court's factual finding on the subtenancy induction.

landlord.identity_basis: The landlord whose consent was required.

written_consent_document.identity_basis: No such document exists in the record.

evidence.proposition: The record contains no evidence showing that the landlord gave written consent to the appellant's induction as subtenant.
evidence.stage: classification of tenancy and interpretation of limitation
evidence.application: The Supreme Court explicitly states there is no evidence to show the appellant was inducted with the written consent of the landlord.

R02.P2.stage: classification of tenancy and interpretation of limitation
R02.P2.basis: Supreme Court's evidentiary assessment regarding lack of written consent.

tenant.identity_basis: The appellant became the direct tenant.

landlord.identity_basis: The landlord who accepted the appellant.

property.value: Cottage at No. 1, Hailey Road, New Delhi

effective_date.identity_basis: The date from which the appellant was accepted as direct tenant.

evidence.proposition: After Brook surrendered the head tenancy, the landlord expressly accepted the appellant as direct tenant from May 1, 1955.
evidence.stage: classification of tenancy and interpretation of limitation
evidence.application: The Supreme Court recognizes the admitted position that the landlord accepted the appellant as direct tenant effective May 1, 1955, after Brook's surrender.

R02.P3.stage: classification of tenancy and interpretation of limitation
R02.P3.basis: Supreme Court's recognition of the direct tenancy establishment.

tenant.identity_basis: The appellant was the subject of the lower court's reasoning.

earlier_letting_date.identity_basis: The date used by lower courts as the start of limitation.

interpreting_courts.identity_basis: The courts that adopted the rejected construction.

evidence.proposition: The District Judge adopted the earlier subtenancy or first letting as the starting point for calculating the appellant's limitation period, and the High Court substantially endorsed that reasoning.
evidence.application: The Supreme Court reports that the District Judge held the petition barred because the tenancy commenced on Sept 1, 1954, and the High Court agreed with this view.

R03.P1.basis: Supreme Court's report of the lower courts' reasoning.

earlier_event.identity_basis: The event used by lower courts as the controlling letting.

later_event.value: Recognition of direct tenancy on May 1, 1955
later_event.identity_basis: The later event of direct tenancy recognition.

governing_limitation_date.identity_basis: The date proposed by lower courts as the governing limitation start.

evidence.proposition: The September 1, 1954 induction as Brook's subtenant is legally the controlling letting for the appellant's Section 11(b) application after direct tenancy was recognized from May 1, 1955.
evidence.application: The Supreme Court reports the lower courts' view that the earlier subtenancy date controlled the limitation period, a view the Supreme Court explicitly rejected.

R03.P2.basis: Supreme Court's report of the lower courts' legal interpretation.

property.value: Cottage at No. 1, Hailey Road, New Delhi

contractual_monthly_rent.identity_basis: The agreed monthly rent stated in the plaint/agreement.

evidence.proposition: The evidence establishes an exact, consistent contractual monthly rent for the demised cottage under the direct tenancy.
evidence.application: The Supreme Court recounts the agreed monthly rent of Rs. 277.50 as the contractual amount.

R04.P1.basis: Supreme Court's recounting of the contractual rent amount.

property.value: Cottage at No. 1, Hailey Road, New Delhi
property.identity_basis: The property for which standard rent was determined.

operative_standard_rent.identity_basis: The standard rent fixed by the trial court.

contractual_rent.identity_basis: The contractual rent to be compared.

evidence.proposition: The legally operative standard rent for the demised cottage has been established through the required adjudication, allowing comparison with the contractual amount.
evidence.application: The Supreme Court reports that the trial court fixed the standard rent at Rs. 855/- p.a., which allows comparison with the contractual rent.

R04.P2.basis: Supreme Court's report of the trial court's standard rent determination.

landlord.identity_basis: The landlord who filed the eviction suit.

tenant.identity_basis: The appellant was the tenant in the suit.

notice_date.identity_basis: The date of the demand notice served.

suit.identity_basis: The eviction suit filed by the landlord.

evidence.proposition: The landlord brought a possession suit asserting failure to pay rent after the statutory demand notice under Section 13(1)(a).
evidence.application: The Supreme Court reports that the landlord filed Civil Suit No. 231/56 on July 3, 1956, asserting default in rent payment after a notice dated May 10, 1956.

R05.P1.basis: Supreme Court's report of the landlord's claim and suit details.

tenant.identity_basis: The appellant failed to pay/tender arrears timely.

lawful_arrears.identity_basis: The specific amount is not quantified in the source text as a fixed proposition.

notice_date.identity_basis: The date of the demand notice.

payment_or_tender_date.value: 1st day of hearing in the trial court
payment_or_tender_date.identity_basis: The date the tenant deposited the arrears, which was after the one-month window.

evidence.proposition: The underlying statutory default occurred: the tenant neither paid nor tendered all legally payable arrears within one month after service of the qualifying demand notice.
evidence.application: The Supreme Court recounts that the tenant deposited the arrears on the first day of the hearing, which was outside the one-month window following the May 10, 1956 notice.

R05.P2.basis: Supreme Court's factual account of the timing of the deposit relative to the notice.

deposit.value: All the arrears of rent as claimed by the plaintiff-landlord
deposit.identity_basis: The amount deposited by the tenant.

deposit_date.value: 1st day of hearing in the trial court
deposit_date.identity_basis: The date the deposit was made.

evidence.proposition: During the eviction proceedings, the tenant deposited the arrears claimed by the landlord.
evidence.application: The Supreme Court states that the appellant deposited all the arrears claimed by the landlord on the first day of the hearing in the trial court.

R05.P3.basis: Supreme Court's factual account of the rent deposit.

coverage_limits: The judgment does not establish the final amount of standard rent as it was remanded for determination.
The judgment does not finally decide whether the landlord was entitled to eviction on the merits, only that the procedural ground for striking off defense was invalid.
